A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete, readable 23-page versions of the same work. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison, including material moved or renumbered in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark evaluations, reinforcement fine-tuning experiments, ablations, and analyses of intermediate diffusion predictions, including appendix results.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results, reports corrected LLaDA-1.5 evaluations, and adds joint multi-task training results in Table S2.

M1.justification: Section 4.2 and Equation 5 change the stated GRPO rollout distribution from the current policy to the old policy. This is a limited correction to the specified training procedure; temporal voting, TSE, and the composite reward formula remain unchanged. The PDFs do not establish whether the training implementation changed.

E1.justification: Both versions cover GSM8K, MATH500, SVAMP, Countdown, and Sudoku, with s1K used for supervised fine-tuning. The new joint-training experiment combines existing tasks without adding datasets or task requirements. Sudoku results are relocated, not newly introduced.

E2.justification: The base/SFT baselines and accuracy-reward comparator d1 are retained. The new joint-training experiment uses the same RFT comparator set. Corrected scores and backbone loading do not introduce a different comparison method.

E3.justification: Appendix G reports correcting evaluation of LLaDA-1.5-trained LoRA adapters, previously loaded into LLaDA, by using the proper LLaDA-1.5 backbone. This affects central RFT comparisons and scoring-rule ablations. Appendix F.1 also introduces joint training on equally sized subsamples from four tasks.

E4.justification: Appendix F.1 adds a focused generalization analysis testing whether one jointly trained model retains benefits across four tasks. Existing voting-weight, entropy, post-RFT voting, and Sudoku failure analyses remain. The scoring-rule ablation is updated under the corrected evaluation backbone.

E5.justification: No run-count, seed, uncertainty-estimation, or significance-testing information is added or revised. New and corrected tables retain point-accuracy reporting, and existing graphical uncertainty displays are unchanged.

E6.justification: Table 2 replaces LLaDA-1.5 RFT results after the backbone correction: combined-reward GSM8K/128 changes from 70.2 to 73.2, while MATH500/128 changes from 30.8 to 29.6. These are corrected evaluations, not same-setting gains or losses. Scoring-rule results also change, and v2 Table S2 adds joint-training results. Voting and Sudoku results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Equation 5 corrects the sampling distribution to the old policy. Section 4.2 and Appendix F.2 also correct the mathematical characterization of the spherical reward: it encourages consistency without penalizing overconfidence in incorrect predictions. The reward formula and other principal definitions remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: temporal oscillation, temporal self-consistency voting, and TSE-based reinforcement. The headline numerical claims are unchanged; the additional experiments support existing contributions.

C2.justification: v2 replaces the misleading calibration explanation with an interpretation of the composite reward as correctness plus temporal consistency. It also fixes the contradictory description of correctness groups in the TSE discussion and adds a multi-task generalization interpretation. Existing Sudoku limitations are retained in Appendix E.

D1.justification: v2 documents the adapter/backbone loading correction and equal-per-task subsampling for joint training. A new reproducibility statement promises release of models and training/inference code upon acceptance. Existing hardware, LoRA settings, training details, and evaluation schedule are retained.

R1.justification: The bibliography contains the same works. Section 2 is condensed while preserving the research positioning relative to diffusion models, self-consistency, semantic entropy, and GRPO-based post-training.

P1.justification: Related work, analyses, methods, and experimental discussion undergo extensive compression and rewriting. Limitations move from the main text into a reorganized appendix. New LLM-usage and reproducibility disclosures and a changelog further revise the document structure.

P2.justification: v2 adds the joint-training table, relocates and renumbers existing appendix tables, shortens captions, and reflows figures within the condensed text. Existing figure graphics and established table formats are retained.

improvement.justification: Correcting the adapter/backbone mismatch repairs an important validity problem in the central LLaDA-1.5 comparisons and scoring-rule ablations. v2 also corrects the GRPO formulation and misleading reward-calibration explanation, substantially improving reliability. The new multi-task discussion overstates uniform improvement—Table S2 includes 28.2 versus a 29.0 baseline on LLaDA-1.5 MATH500/128—but this limited overstatement does not outweigh the substantive corrections.
